item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The concept is good, but the writing really doesn't do it for me.
Numerous examples:

//"…pair of of flood lamps used in photography…" => "pair of flood lamps of a type typically used in photography". These lamps - the ones being contained - are not being used in photography, so don't say that they are.

"…however each lamp will display the shadow of an unidentified young woman…" But this is inconsistent with the content of the observation log, which reveals that additional humanoid shadows will appear. Also, a lamp doesn't "display shadows" in any meaningful sense. Perhaps "…however each lamp will cause shadows not corresponding to physical objects in the room to appear on the screen" would be better.

"… Whether or not this shadow corresponds to anyone living or dead has yet to be determined, although the shadow appears to re-enact a specific series of events leading up to the woman's death." Not necessary, and kind of takes some of the punch out of the narrative arc of the observation log. I'd recommend cutting.

"SCP-205 will display a still image of one woman in a provocative pose." SCP-205 is the pair of lamps, so it isn't displaying an image. "The screen in the containment chamber will show a shadow resembling…" may be better. Also, "provocative pose" is not the best phrase: it could mean anything from a sexually suggestive pose to a rude gesture.

"…the individual displayed appears to be distinct and consistent through all cycles". I don't know what you're trying to say here.

"…any movement of the atmosphere…". "Atmosphere" is the wrong word here; "air" would be clearer.

And so on. I'd urge a top-to-bottom re-write. The clinical tone may also be improved by presenting the observation log in tabular form with time-stamps.

I acknowledge that this sound a bit harsh and out-of-place, given that this is already one of the highest-ranked articles on the site, but there you have it.

item.content:encoded:
trimming it down i'd leave up to you, but i strongly suggest moving these parts:

For the first month of operation, SCP-205 will display a still image of one woman in a provocative pose.

and

During the last week of the first month, the shadow will begin to move slightly as if the individual is shifting her weight or becoming uncomfortable. Her hair and clothing will be observed to flutter in ways that do not correspond to any movement of the atmosphere within Chamber 52. By the end of the first calendar month the shadow will break her pose and spend the next eight hours moving through a series of poses that imply a photography session complete with clothing changes and short breaks, sometimes including a meal.

After this session is over the shadow will constantly be in motion for the next five months, displaying a pantomime of the last days of a young model's life before she is brutally murdered at the end of the cycle. The shadow of the woman never moves beyond the boundaries of the projection screen. The shadows of objects that the woman appears to be interacting with do not appear unless they are being picked up or carried, and with the exception of the final month of the cycle any other individuals that the shadow appears to be interacting with are not seen.

to the start of the overview. the result is the description only talks about the setup and what happens when the lights go out, all the information you need. all actual events happening during the cycle are covered in the overview.

other than that, it is definitely a bit long, with giant paragraphs. my kind of thing really, i love giving entirely too much detail, but for the sake of people being willing to read it it's definitely worth trying to trim down as much as possible.

i love this one though, awesome work.
